toolu_019Dr5VWw8KKu86Re5SDY1Fo.command: cd /Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src && grep -n "export function layers" -A 30 build.mjs | head -n 50

content.text: The library treats an array whose first item is a string as one layer of rows. My calls wrapped every row in its own array, so each row became a separate y level. The barrels, table post and candle landed at y 8..12 instead of their intended levels. I'll pass each level as a flat list of row strings.

input.summary: room-18 (owner upper bedrooms) now writes only its own cells: 16 placed, no refusals, no off-palette blocks. The cause was that each row was passed as its own y layer in layers(), so barrels, table post and candle were placed at y 8..12 instead of their levels.
left: Other parts still report refusals and off-palette blocks (roofs, openings, chimneys, cart lean-to) and the flight landing at 86,7,9 has no headroom. Those belong to other parts and were not touched.

The three beds were placed by bed(), which returns false silently when blocked; the count of 16 matches all three beds (6 cells) so they landed, but the bed helper's result is not checked in the part.

waste.what: Misread layers() rowsOrLayers shape: wrapped each row in its own array, so every row became its own y layer. Barrels, table post, candle and lantern were written at the wrong heights, and two of them hit earlier parts' cells at y 12.
waste.cost: One full ./make.sh run (about a minute) plus reading the library's layers() source to confirm the shape rule, then one edit across three calls and a rebuild.
waste.tool: A layers() guard that throws when a row count or row width doesn't match the origin box, or a per-part report of writes outside the part's declared box (here y 7..9, x 86..91, z 10..14). Either would have pointed at the wrong y at once. The doc comment should state the single-layer form (flat array of row strings) next to the multi-layer form.

waste.what: Working out the expected placed count by hand (6 + 3 + 1 + 6 = 16) to confirm the layers and beds landed as planned.
waste.cost: Mental arithmetic on the layer strings; no tool run.
waste.tool: A per-layer census in the part report (cells written per y level, with the block at each cell) would show this without counting.
